findings.classification: documentation clarity; unavailable prerequisite separately recorded
findings.title: Required Python version and setup command do not line up
findings.observed: Guide says You need Python 3.12 for the pinned Schemathesis environment below, then uses python -m venv. Tool page says the pinned 4.33.1 example requires Python 3.11 or newer. On this machine python is 3.13.15, so the literal venv command creates a different runtime without checking it.
findings.impact: Reader cannot tell whether 3.12 is a strict requirement or only the recorded runtime. A successful generic command does not establish the advertised environment. This walkthrough needed an explicitly labeled compatibility decision before proceeding.
findings.smallest_useful_fix: Distinguish supported Python versions from the tested 3.12 environment. If 3.12 is required, show an interpreter-selection/version-check step before venv creation and state what to do when it is missing.
findings.confidence: high for wording and observed interpreter behavior; no claim that Python 3.13 is unsupported

findings.classification: usability improvement, recovered through linked official documentation
findings.title: The first exercise lacks a short transition to the reader's API
findings.observed: Wiki shows a fixture wrapper invocation whose exposed inputs are only --port and --output. It describes selected positive server-error checks, then links a broad CLI reference. To address the scenario's invalid-input testing or a different API, this walkthrough read the wrapper and combined LOCATION/--url/filters/--mode/--checks/report options from two external reference pages.
findings.impact: The toy finding is easy to reproduce, but the reader must design the next command and realize positive-only not_a_server_error does not check invalid-input rejection. The linked references do provide the missing mechanics, so this is recoverable friction, not a dead-end or broken command.
findings.smallest_useful_fix: Add a compact Adapt to your API section with a PowerShell command using a reader-supplied schema location and loopback test URL, one explicit operation filter, budget/report settings, and a sentence explaining when to use negative/all generation plus negative_data_rejection.
findings.confidence: high for missing on-page command and wrapper interface; severity is an expert usability judgment

overall_outcome.summary: The wiki selected an appropriate tool and supplied a usable bounded exercise. Both replay and Schemathesis finding/correction succeeded in a labeled Python 3.13 recovery. The exact documented Python 3.12 route was unavailable, repository acquisition was bypassed using the provided checkout, and own-API adaptation required linked external references.
overall_outcome.first_attempt: Tool selection and fixture discovery passed; exact Python 3.12 scanner setup blocked by unavailable interpreter.
overall_outcome.recovery: Tool-page Python 3.11+ compatibility justified a fresh Python 3.13.15 venv. All supplied pins installed; faulty run produced expected ST101; corrected run completed selected scope.
overall_outcome.cleanup: All own target sessions stopped with Ctrl+C; no listener on 8771 afterward.

unavailable_prerequisites.handling: Stopped exact documented-environment route; did not install a system runtime. Completed labeled Python 3.13 recovery based on tool-page compatibility.

unverified_or_lower_confidence_observati: Guide says Work from a local copy of the ToolWiki repository and links GitHub, but does not include a clone/download-and-cd command. Existing checkout was an audit shortcut, so acquisition difficulty was not actually tested and is not a confirmed blocker.

API guide says finding review guide explains implementation/schema/setup decisions; destination is generic and its worked examples concern source warnings and advisories. The existing general guidance plus fixture explanation was sufficient for this result; no separate defect is asserted.

result_interpretation.faulty: Schema permits quantity 0, so HTTP 500 is an implementation failure for a valid input, not evidence of invalid-input acceptance. Replay and scanner independently reproduce the same response.
result_interpretation.corrected: The fixed service accepts that same input, returns 201 with total 0/unitPrice 10, and passes six generated positive server-error cases across three operations.
result_interpretation.coverage: Faulty scanner stopped after first failure with two operations skipped. Corrected scanner tested all selected operations, but examples, fuzzing and stateful phases were disabled. These outcomes do not establish full API correctness or security.
result_interpretation.failure_classes: A refused connection concerns service readiness/port; schema-load/configuration failure concerns scanner setup; ST101 after successful schema loading and an observed 500 is a finding. Replay exit 0 and scanner exit 1 mean different things, as documented.
result_interpretation.own_api_adaptation: Obtain an accurate definition and reachable disposable service, choose schema LOCATION and explicit test base URL, limit operations and budget, choose checks and positive/negative generation intentionally, configure auth/state if needed, and retain comparable reports. Linked official docs supplied command option details. No credential or real-service adaptation was executed.

evidence.sanitization: Human-authored report and retained text are ASCII. Non-ASCII scanner glyphs are represented as literal backslash-u escapes; terminal controls are removed. Manifest preserves hashes of original and retained content. Tool-generated temporary raw reports were not edited.
